transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess I came in because I just can’t seem to stop worrying. It’s like everything is happening in my head at the same time, all the time. My marriage, whether I’m messing things up at work or falling behind, bills, stuff around the house that I keep starting and then dropping, and then I start thinking maybe I’m just failing in general — as a husband, as a father, as the person who’s supposed to keep things together.

It’s not one specific thing, really. It’s more like my mind keeps scanning for what I’ve forgotten or what’s about to go wrong, and then it lands on something else before I can even deal with the first thing. I work with computers, so I’m used to juggling details, but lately it feels like I’m juggling my whole life and I’m dropping pieces everywhere. And I know some of it probably sounds like normal adult stuff, but it feels constant, like I can’t get any space from it.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yeah. Very hard. That’s actually one of the things that scares me, because I can sometimes see that I’m doing it — like I’ll literally tell myself, “Okay, stop, just focus on the code in front of you,” or if I’m exercising I’ll try to just breathe and count reps or whatever — and it doesn’t really stop.

It’s like one concern catches onto another one. I’ll start with something small, like maybe I’m behind on a task or I didn’t explain something clearly at work, and then within a few minutes I’m twenty steps ahead. I’m imagining getting a bad review, then losing my job, then not being able to support my family, and then it becomes this whole thing where I’m the reason everything falls apart. And I know, logically, that I jumped way ahead, but knowing that doesn’t make it shut off. It feels like once it gets going, I’m just along for the ride.
Before these worries became a problem, did you already have trouble with focus or finishing tasks going back to childhood?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I had this same kind of problem going all the way back to childhood, at least not in a way that anyone flagged or that I remember as a major thing.

I mean, I was probably a normal kid in terms of procrastinating sometimes or not wanting to do homework, and I’m sure I had unfinished stuff here and there, but I don’t remember it being this pattern where I just couldn’t focus or couldn’t finish anything no matter what. I got through school, and later college and grad school, so… I don’t know. It’s hard to separate what was just normal kid behavior from something meaningful.

If anything, the trouble now feels tied up with all the worrying and second-guessing. But as far as childhood, I don’t have a clear memory of having a long-standing focus problem before all this.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

It wasn’t like one single event where I can say, “That day changed everything.” It was more that things started building up, and then at some point I realized I’d been living like this for months.

I’d say it’s been about nine months now. Around when the cloud migration at work really ramped up — that became this constant pressure, a lot of moving parts and things that could go wrong — and at the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular. Not just one bad fight, but this pattern where it felt like there was always tension waiting for me in one place or the other.

So… I don’t know if I’d call it a specific event exactly. More like work got heavier, home got harder, and since then the worrying just hasn’t really let up.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that from everything else. I wouldn’t say I’m… depressed in the sense of feeling sad all day or like there’s this heavy dark mood constantly, at least I don’t think so.

I do feel worn down a lot, and sometimes kind of discouraged, like I’m tired of my own brain and tired of feeling like I can’t get a normal amount of peace. But when you say “down or depressed,” I’m not sure if that counts or if that’s more just being stressed and exhausted. I haven’t really been thinking of myself as depressed, exactly. More like overwhelmed.
Do you feel like your worrying is excessive compared with the actual problems going on?

Yeah… I think that’s honestly why I came in. It feels excessive, even if some of the problems are real. Like, yes, there are things going on — my marriage has been tense, work has been a lot, money and bills are always kind of in the back of my head, and there are house projects I’ve started and then dropped. So it’s not like I’m worrying about absolutely nothing.

But the amount of worrying feels out of proportion. It’s like all of it is happening at once in my head, all the time. I’ll be thinking about whether I’m slipping at work, and then it turns into whether I’m going to mess something up badly, and then somehow that connects to whether I’m failing at home, or failing as a husband, or as a father. And then I’m thinking about bills, and the house, and all the things I haven’t finished, and it just keeps stacking up.

So… yeah. The problems are there, but my reaction to them feels bigger than the actual situation sometimes. I can’t seem to put any of it down.
Are you worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly about the problems at work and home?

Yeah, definitely. It’s not just work and home, though those are the big obvious ones. It’s like once my brain gets going, it pulls in everything else too.

I’ll start with something concrete, like whether I’m keeping up at work, and then it spreads into, “Am I slipping? Are people noticing? Am I going to drop something important?” Then I’ll come home and it’s the marriage stuff, like replaying conversations or worrying that I’m making things worse. And then suddenly I’m thinking about bills, and the house projects I keep starting and not finishing, and whether I’m basically failing as a husband and father.

That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. It feels like I can’t stop worrying about everything at once. Even when one thing settles down for a minute, another thing just takes its place.
Even when things are relatively calm, do you still find yourself worrying a lot?

Yeah. That’s actually one of the things that makes it feel so frustrating, because even if nothing is actively blowing up in that moment, my mind doesn’t really seem to accept that as a reason to calm down.

Like, I could be sitting there and technically everything is fine — no immediate crisis, nobody’s calling me, nothing has happened right then — and I’ll still be going through this whole rotation in my head. My marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, the house, the projects I keep starting and then just dropping, and then it turns into this bigger thing of, “Am I failing as a husband? Am I failing as a father?” It’s like my brain keeps looking for the next thing to latch onto.

That’s a big part of why I came in. It’s not just that I worry when there’s a clear problem. It’s that I can’t stop worrying about everything at once, even when things are relatively calm.
Do you have trouble relaxing?

Yeah. Very much so. I don’t really feel like I relax anymore in the normal sense of the word.

It’s like my body is wound tight almost all day. Even if I’m just sitting at my computer or I’m between tasks, my shoulders are up and locked, and I’ll realize I’m sort of bracing, like something is about to happen. Sometimes I don’t even notice it until I let out a breath or my neck starts hurting and I’m like, okay, I’ve apparently been sitting here like I’m waiting for bad news.

And sitting still is hard. Between meetings, I’ll get up and pace around, not even going anywhere useful, just back and forth. Or if I’m at chess club, which should be quiet and focused, I’ll catch myself tapping pieces or moving my hands around because just sitting there calmly feels almost impossible. It’s embarrassing because I’m aware of it, but I can’t seem to settle my body down.

So yeah, I have a lot of trouble relaxing. Even when I’m supposed to be doing nothing, I feel like I’m still on alert.
Have these worries been going on for more than 6 months?

Yeah… definitely more than six months. I’d say it’s been about nine months now, give or take.

It really seemed to start when the cloud migration at work ramped up. At first I told myself it was just a busy project phase and it would calm down once that got under control, but around the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular too. So it wasn’t just a rough week or even a rough month — it kind of became this constant background thing.

Looking back, I can mark it pretty clearly from then. Since that whole period started, I don’t think I’ve really gone back to feeling normal for any real stretch of time.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I don’t think it’s that I’ve lost interest exactly. I still know, in my head, what kinds of things I usually like or want to do.

It’s more that I don’t always feel like I can fully get into them, if that makes sense. Like if something is supposed to be enjoyable, I might still show up for it or start doing it, but I’m not necessarily relaxed enough to really enjoy it the way I used to. But I don’t know if that’s the same as losing pleasure, or if it’s just me being distracted and tense.

So… I wouldn’t say I’ve completely stopped caring about the things I enjoy. I just don’t feel as present with them lately.
Have you been feeling sad or low most of the day?

I don’t think so… not most of the day, no.

I mean, I get worn down and discouraged sometimes, especially when I feel like I can’t get a handle on things, but I wouldn’t describe it as being sad all day or waking up feeling depressed and staying that way. It’s more like I’m tense or preoccupied, and then I might feel low for a bit because I’m tired of feeling that way.

But if you mean a constant sadness that’s there for most of the day, most days… I don’t think that’s really what’s happening.
Is this worry causing problems in your daily life?

Yeah… it is. I wish I could say it’s just something I’m feeling internally and I’m still keeping everything together, but it’s starting to show up in places I can’t really explain away anymore.

At work, for example, my manager has started actually documenting things I’ve missed — like architectural details that I normally would catch or at least follow up on. That’s been… honestly pretty embarrassing, because my job depends on being able to think clearly and keep track of those moving parts. And it’s not like I don’t care. I care a lot. But I’ll be reviewing something and my mind is already running through ten other concerns, and then later someone points out that I missed a dependency or didn’t think through part of the design carefully enough.

And at home, it’s causing problems too. I keep starting things and then leaving them half-finished, or I’m physically there but distracted enough that it’s obvious. Then that turns into an argument, or makes an argument worse, because I’m not really present or I seem like I’m not listening. So, yes… it’s definitely affecting daily life. It’s not just in my head anymore.
If the work and home stress were to improve, do you think the worrying would mostly go away?

Honestly, no… I don’t think it would mostly go away. I mean, it would help, obviously. If work calmed down and things at home felt more stable, I’d probably have less immediate stuff to spiral about.

But the problem is it doesn’t feel like the worry is only about one situation. It’s like everything stacks up at once. I came in because I feel like I can’t stop worrying about all of it — my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep starting and then dropping, and then this bigger fear that I’m basically failing as a husband and father.

So even if one part improved, I think my mind would just move to the next thing. Like, okay, work is better, but what about money? Or the house? Or am I still not doing enough at home? It feels less like one stressor causing the worry and more like the worry just keeps finding things to attach itself to.
Have you been more irritable than usual?

I’m not completely sure, honestly. I wouldn’t want to say I’m walking around angry all the time or anything like that.

Maybe I get a little shorter with people than I’d like, but it’s hard for me to separate whether that’s irritability or just being tired and preoccupied. Like, if someone asks me something when I’m already mentally tangled up, I might answer too sharply and then later feel bad about it. But I haven’t really been keeping track of it as its own thing.

So… maybe somewhat, but I’m not sure it’s one of the main things I’ve noticed.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah. Sleep has been… pretty bad, honestly.

Most nights I’ll feel completely exhausted, like my body is ready to shut down, but then as soon as I’m in bed my brain starts up again. I’ll be lying there going over work risks, things I might have missed, money stuff, and then replaying something I said to my wife — like whether I came across wrong or made things worse. It’s not even productive thinking. It’s just this loop.

And even when I do finally fall asleep, I don’t stay asleep very well. I’ve been waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and once I’m awake, that’s basically it. My mind is already rehearsing tomorrow’s problems before the day has even started, and I can’t get back down from it. So I end up starting the day already drained.
Were the worries already happening before the work and marriage stress began?

I mean… not really in this same way. I’ve always been someone who thinks a lot and probably over-plans, but this level of worrying really started about nine months ago.

That was around when the cloud migration at work ramped up and became this constant pressure, and at the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular. It’s hard to separate the two because they kind of grew together — work got heavier, home got more tense, and then my mind just never seemed to shut off after that. So I wouldn’t say it was already happening like this before then. It’s been about nine months.
Do you feel your anxiety is stronger than would be expected for what’s been going on in your life?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I know there are real things going on, so part of me keeps saying, “Of course you’re worried, these are actual problems.” But the level of it feels bigger than the problems themselves, if that makes sense.

I came in because I can’t seem to stop worrying about everything at once. It’s my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, house projects I keep dropping or never finishing, and then it all turns into this bigger fear that I’m basically failing as a husband and father. It doesn’t stay in one lane. One thought just links to the next, and suddenly I’m not just worried about an argument or a work issue — I’m questioning whether I’m messing up my whole life.

So yes, I think it’s stronger than what would be expected. Or at least it feels like my reaction is way out of proportion and I can’t get it to quiet down.
Aside from work and marriage problems, do you still find yourself worrying a lot about other areas of your life?

Yeah, definitely. It’s not just work and my marriage, even though those are the big obvious ones.

It kind of spreads into everything. I’ll worry about bills, even when I’ve already checked them, or I’ll start thinking about house projects I haven’t finished and feel like I’m falling behind on being a responsible adult. Then that turns into this whole bigger thing where I’m wondering if I’m failing as a husband, or as a father, or just not keeping up with life in general.

It’s like I can’t keep the worries separated. One thing sets it off, and then suddenly I’m worrying about five other areas at once. That’s really why I came in — because I can’t seem to stop worrying about everything all at the same time.
When your mind starts racing, is it usually about the work and marriage stress, or does it also happen when those problems aren’t on your mind?

It happens with the work and marriage stuff a lot, yes, but it’s not only when I’m directly thinking about those problems. That’s kind of the part that scares me, honestly. My mind can start racing and it’ll jump all over the place.

Like, it might start with something from work — wondering if I’m slipping or if I missed something — but then suddenly I’m thinking about bills, or the house projects I keep starting and dropping, or whether I’m doing enough at home. And then it becomes this bigger, ugly thought that I’m basically failing as a husband and father. It doesn’t stay contained.

So even if the original trigger is work or an argument with my wife, once it gets going it turns into everything at once. That’s really why I came in — because I can’t seem to stop worrying, and it feels like my brain is just scanning for the next thing I’m behind on or messing up.

And sitting still is hard. Between meetings, I’ll get up and pace around, not even going anywhere useful, just back and forth. Or if I’m at chess club, which should be quiet and focused, I’ll catch myself tapping pieces or moving my hands around because just sitting there calmly feels almost impossible. It’s embarrassing because I’m aware of it, but I can’t seem to settle my body down.

So yeah, I have a lot of trouble relaxing. Even when I’m supposed to be doing nothing, I feel like I’m still on alert.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms have been present for at least 6 months, which is key to distinguishing generalized anxiety disorder from adjustment disorder and other unspecified conditions.
doctor.question: Have these worries been going on for more than 6 months?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about nine months, since the cloud migration ramped up and the arguments at home started becoming a regular thing.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the worries have been going on and whether they exceed 6 months, which directly matches the duration profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… definitely more than six months. I’d say it’s been about nine months now, give or take.

It really seemed to start when the cloud migration at work ramped up. At first I told myself it was just a busy project phase and it would calm down once that got under control, but around the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular too. So it wasn’t just a rough week or even a rough month — it kind of became this constant background thing.

Looking back, I can mark it pretty clearly from then. Since that whole period started, I don’t think I’ve really gone back to feeling normal for any real stretch of time.

doctor.intent: Assess whether depressive symptoms include loss of interest or pleasure, to distinguish generalized anxiety disorder from a depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest or pleasure, which is not covered by any listed symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I don’t think it’s that I’ve lost interest exactly. I still know, in my head, what kinds of things I usually like or want to do.

It’s more that I don’t always feel like I can fully get into them, if that makes sense. Like if something is supposed to be enjoyable, I might still show up for it or start doing it, but I’m not necessarily relaxed enough to really enjoy it the way I used to. But I don’t know if that’s the same as losing pleasure, or if it’s just me being distracted and tense.

So… I wouldn’t say I’ve completely stopped caring about the things I enjoy. I just don’t feel as present with them lately.

doctor.intent: Assess whether core depressive symptom of persistent low mood is present to distinguish generalized anxiety disorder from a depressive disorder or adjustment disorder with depressed mood.
doctor.question: Have you been feeling sad or low most of the day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressed mood or feeling sad/low most of the day, which is not covered by the provided GAD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not most of the day, no.

I mean, I get worn down and discouraged sometimes, especially when I feel like I can’t get a handle on things, but I wouldn’t describe it as being sad all day or waking up feeling depressed and staying that way. It’s more like I’m tense or preoccupied, and then I might feel low for a bit because I’m tired of feeling that way.

But if you mean a constant sadness that’s there for most of the day, most days… I don’t think that’s really what’s happening.

inference.note: F32.A dropped: patient denies persistent low mood and anhedonia; symptoms are predominantly excessive, hard-to-control worry across multiple domains for >6 months with restlessness/tension, most consistent with GAD. Adjustment disorder remains possible given onset amid stressors, though breadth, persistence, and occurrence even when calm favor F41.1.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms are causing clinically significant impairment, which helps distinguish generalized anxiety disorder from a milder unspecified anxiety presentation.
doctor.question: Is this worry causing problems in your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My manager has started documenting missed architectural details, and at home I’m leaving projects half-finished and showing up distracted enough that the arguments keep escalating.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the worry is causing problems in daily life, which directly corresponds to functional impairment from the anxiety.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it is. I wish I could say it’s just something I’m feeling internally and I’m still keeping everything together, but it’s starting to show up in places I can’t really explain away anymore.

At work, for example, my manager has started actually documenting things I’ve missed — like architectural details that I normally would catch or at least follow up on. That’s been… honestly pretty embarrassing, because my job depends on being able to think clearly and keep track of those moving parts. And it’s not like I don’t care. I care a lot. But I’ll be reviewing something and my mind is already running through ten other concerns, and then later someone points out that I missed a dependency or didn’t think through part of the design carefully enough.

And at home, it’s causing problems too. I keep starting things and then leaving them half-finished, or I’m physically there but distracted enough that it’s obvious. Then that turns into an argument, or makes an argument worse, because I’m not really present or I seem like I’m not listening. So, yes… it’s definitely affecting daily life. It’s not just in my head anymore.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the anxiety is specifically tied to an identifiable stressor, which would help distinguish adjustment disorder with anxiety from generalized anxiety disorder.
doctor.question: If the work and home stress were to improve, do you think the worrying would mostly go away?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can't stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I'm slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep dropping, and whether I'm basically failing as a husband and father.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the worrying is mainly tied to specific current stressors or whether it reflects a broader, persistent pattern of excessive worry.

patient.answer:
Honestly, no… I don’t think it would mostly go away. I mean, it would help, obviously. If work calmed down and things at home felt more stable, I’d probably have less immediate stuff to spiral about.

But the problem is it doesn’t feel like the worry is only about one situation. It’s like everything stacks up at once. I came in because I feel like I can’t stop worrying about all of it — my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep starting and then dropping, and then this bigger fear that I’m basically failing as a husband and father.

So even if one part improved, I think my mind would just move to the next thing. Like, okay, work is better, but what about money? Or the house? Or am I still not doing enough at home? It feels less like one stressor causing the worry and more like the worry just keeps finding things to attach itself to.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has frequent irritability, a core associated symptom that would further support generalized anxiety disorder over adjustment disorder or unspecified anxiety disorder.
doctor.question: Have you been more irritable than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about irritability, but the provided symptom profile does not include an irritability symptom item.

patient.answer:
I’m not completely sure, honestly. I wouldn’t want to say I’m walking around angry all the time or anything like that.

Maybe I get a little shorter with people than I’d like, but it’s hard for me to separate whether that’s irritability or just being tired and preoccupied. Like, if someone asks me something when I’m already mentally tangled up, I might answer too sharply and then later feel bad about it. But I haven’t really been keeping track of it as its own thing.

So… maybe somewhat, but I’m not sure it’s one of the main things I’ve noticed.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has the key remaining GAD symptom of sleep disturbance to further confirm generalized anxiety disorder over adjustment disorder or unspecified anxiety disorder.
doctor.question: Have you been having trouble sleeping?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Most nights I lie in bed exhausted but my brain keeps running through work risks, money, and what I said to my wife, and even when I do fall asleep I wake up around 3 or 4 and can't get back down because I'm already rehearsing tomorrow's problems.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about trouble sleeping, which matches the sleep disturbance symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah. Sleep has been… pretty bad, honestly.

Most nights I’ll feel completely exhausted, like my body is ready to shut down, but then as soon as I’m in bed my brain starts up again. I’ll be lying there going over work risks, things I might have missed, money stuff, and then replaying something I said to my wife — like whether I came across wrong or made things worse. It’s not even productive thinking. It’s just this loop.

And even when I do finally fall asleep, I don’t stay asleep very well. I’ve been waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and once I’m awake, that’s basically it. My mind is already rehearsing tomorrow’s problems before the day has even started, and I can’t get back down from it. So I end up starting the day already drained.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the anxiety is primarily tied to an identifiable stressor, which would support adjustment disorder versus generalized anxiety disorder or unspecified anxiety disorder.
doctor.question: Were the worries already happening before the work and marriage stress began?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about nine months, since the cloud migration ramped up and the arguments at home started becoming a regular thing.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timeline/onset of the worries relative to work and marriage stress, which is most directly covered by the duration profile.

patient.answer:
I mean… not really in this same way. I’ve always been someone who thinks a lot and probably over-plans, but this level of worrying really started about nine months ago.

That was around when the cloud migration at work ramped up and became this constant pressure, and at the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular. It’s hard to separate the two because they kind of grew together — work got heavier, home got more tense, and then my mind just never seemed to shut off after that. So I wouldn’t say it was already happening like this before then. It’s been about nine months.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the anxiety is clearly out of proportion to the identifiable stressors, which best distinguishes generalized anxiety disorder from adjustment disorder at this stage.
doctor.question: Do you feel your anxiety is stronger than would be expected for what’s been going on in your life?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can't stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I'm slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep dropping, and whether I'm basically failing as a husband and father.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the level of anxiety is excessive or disproportionate to current life stressors, which directly matches excessive anxiety and worry.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I mean, I know there are real things going on, so part of me keeps saying, “Of course you’re worried, these are actual problems.” But the level of it feels bigger than the problems themselves, if that makes sense.

I came in because I can’t seem to stop worrying about everything at once. It’s my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, house projects I keep dropping or never finishing, and then it all turns into this bigger fear that I’m basically failing as a husband and father. It doesn’t stay in one lane. One thought just links to the next, and suddenly I’m not just worried about an argument or a work issue — I’m questioning whether I’m messing up my whole life.

So yes, I think it’s stronger than what would be expected. Or at least it feels like my reaction is way out of proportion and I can’t get it to quiet down.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the anxiety is focused on a specific identifiable stressor versus generalized across many domains, to distinguish adjustment disorder with anxiety from generalized anxiety disorder.
doctor.question: Aside from work and marriage problems, do you still find yourself worrying a lot about other areas of your life?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can't stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I'm slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep dropping, and whether I'm basically failing as a husband and father.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the worry extends beyond work and marriage into multiple other life areas, which directly assesses excessive anxiety and worry about a number of events or activities.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely. It’s not just work and my marriage, even though those are the big obvious ones.

It kind of spreads into everything. I’ll worry about bills, even when I’ve already checked them, or I’ll start thinking about house projects I haven’t finished and feel like I’m falling behind on being a responsible adult. Then that turns into this whole bigger thing where I’m wondering if I’m failing as a husband, or as a father, or just not keeping up with life in general.

It’s like I can’t keep the worries separated. One thing sets it off, and then suddenly I’m worrying about five other areas at once. That’s really why I came in — because I can’t seem to stop worrying about everything all at the same time.

doctor.intent: Differentiate generalized anxiety disorder from adjustment disorder by clarifying whether the anxiety is confined to the identifiable stressors or persists independently of them.
doctor.question: When your mind starts racing, is it usually about the work and marriage stress, or does it also happen when those problems aren’t on your mind?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can't stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I'm slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep dropping, and whether I'm basically failing as a husband and father.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the racing thoughts and worry are limited to work and marriage stress or occur across other situations too, which directly concerns excessive worry about multiple areas of life.

patient.answer:
It happens with the work and marriage stuff a lot, yes, but it’s not only when I’m directly thinking about those problems. That’s kind of the part that scares me, honestly. My mind can start racing and it’ll jump all over the place.

Like, it might start with something from work — wondering if I’m slipping or if I missed something — but then suddenly I’m thinking about bills, or the house projects I keep starting and dropping, or whether I’m doing enough at home. And then it becomes this bigger, ugly thought that I’m basically failing as a husband and father. It doesn’t stay contained.

So even if the original trigger is work or an argument with my wife, once it gets going it turns into everything at once. That’s really why I came in — because I can’t seem to stop worrying, and it feels like my brain is just scanning for the next thing I’m behind on or messing up.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes excessive, difficult-to-control anxiety and worry about multiple domains of life occurring for about 9 months, persisting even when things are calm, and accompanied by restlessness, muscle tension, impaired relaxation, and significant sleep disturbance, with clear occupational and family impairment. This pattern is broader and more persistent than an adjustment reaction and is more specifically consistent with generalized anxiety disorder rather than unspecified anxiety disorder.
